slots.line: The rules every sheet shares — box sizing, rhythm resets, the drawn-size rules for charts and diagrams.
The page's grid: the prose column and how far a figure may break out of it.
How body text reads — headings, lists, quotes, links.
Inline code, code blocks and tables.
The fourteen primitives: callouts, figures, stats, steps, FAQs.
The top of a post — title, eyebrow, subtitle, byline, cover image.
The site header — name, logo, tagline, menu.
An archive's page: its heading and the line under it. The rows are `entries`.
A list of posts — on the index, a term, an author.
The end of a post — terms, source link, author.
The page of a site's own type, drawn from the fields it marks `role:` fact, kicker, flag.
Footnotes — cards at the end, or notes in the margin.
The logo wall — a row, or a marquee.
Transitions and entrances — none, a glide, a reveal.
A drawn background behind the page.

sets.name: light-serif
sets.line: A warm paper, a text serif, an oxblood link — the reading page.

sets.name: dark-sans
sets.line: A near-black, a grotesk, one cool blue — the tool at night.

sets.name: loud-accent
sets.line: White, a wide display grotesk, one hot red that has to carry the page.

sets.name: committed
sets.line: The page drenched in one saturated cobalt, a display serif, a yellow that answers it.

sets.name: pathological
sets.line: Everything a piece might assume, broken — big body, huge condensed heads, a narrow column, square corners, tight leading.

house/house.line: The fifteen rules editorial, technical, studio and folio all carry, verbatim — box sizing, the rhythm reset, hairlines, and the drawn size of charts, diagrams and flows.
house/house.name: house

column/three-track.line: One grid, three tracks — text, breakout, full. Prose in the text track; charts, diagrams and wide figures break out by `measure.breakout`.

rhythm.description: The gap between two blocks: `loose` is space.4, four fifths of a line; `tight` is space.3, for reference that is scanned.

data.description: Code blocks and tables take the breakout track too — where data is the content rather than an illustration of it.

fit.description: A chart, diagram or flow shrinks to its drawing and centres on the track, its caption wrapping under the drawing — one left edge per figure.

pages.description: A page's article dissolves into the column as a post's does, so its figures and tables break out of the text track too.

shrink.description: Every block in the column may shrink below its content's width — a long unbroken line scrolls or wraps inside its block instead of widening the track.

column/three-track.name: three-track

prose/book.line: Long-form prose — hyphenated and pretty-wrapped, links underlined at a third of their colour until pointed at, an italic ruled quote.

display-heads.description: The title and section heads in the display face, the title at the face's own weight; the heads under them in the prose face; every head set off by the space above it.

refs.took: a heading is emphasised by the space above it, bold not italic, and only a small step up in size
the headline in a display face at its regular weight, large, carried by size alone

prose/book.name: book

prose/display.line: Display prose — every heading in the display face, bold, tight and balanced; the body in the system sans; a ruled, muted quote.
prose/display.name: display

prose/docs.line: Reference prose — headings in the heading face tracked in, quiet deep-link marks on hover, links underlined from the font, no hyphenation.
prose/docs.name: docs

prose/grotesk.line: Prose under a medium grotesk — headings at one weight, tracked in more as they grow, h4 a shade over the body; links underlined at a third of their colour; a ruled, muted quote.
prose/grotesk.name: grotesk

code/first-class.line: Code and tables as the content, not an aside — inline code bordered like a token, blocks as slabs, tables ruled with tabular figures and zebra rows.
code/first-class.name: first-class

code/quiet.line: Code and tables that defer to the prose — inline code on a tint, blocks as a bordered slab, full-width tables in the UI face with small-caps headers.

display-heads.description: Table headers in the display face and tracked wider — a theme whose chrome is set in it.

code/quiet.name: quiet

code/tint.line: Code on a tint with no borders — inline code and blocks on the surface colour; tables ruled, tabular figures, the header in the display face over a rule in the text colour.
code/tint.name: tint

blocks/hairline.line: The fourteen primitives with no boxes — a hairline above each block, numbers in the display face as large as a heading, `01` steps, pill buttons with an arrow.
blocks/hairline.name: hairline

blocks/ink.line: The fourteen primitives in the text colour alone — no tint, no accent. A callout says how much it matters by how much ink it takes (a grey rule for a tip, a black one for a note, a heavy one for a warning, a danger set in reverse); a summary, a row of figures and a call to action sit between a heavy rule and a light one, as a book sets a table; a pull quote is an epigraph. Right for a writer, a reference or a notebook; wrong for a brand that needs its colour on the page.

refs.took: admonitions in greyscale, heavier as they grow more serious, the most serious one reversed out of black
the epigraph — italic, no quotation marks, the source set right under it — and the booktabs table: a heavy rule above, a light one below, space between rows

blocks/ink.name: ink

blocks/rows.line: The fourteen primitives as ruled rows — no box inside a box, only a hairline above a block or one quiet surface, numbers in the display face, steps and questions as rows under hairlines, one solid button.
blocks/rows.name: rows

blocks/ruled.line: The fourteen primitives as reference — bordered surfaces with an accent rule, mono figures, numbered steps underlined, questions as a folded tree.
blocks/ruled.name: ruled

blocks/surface.line: The fourteen primitives as a magazine sets them — tinted surfaces with an accent rule, italic pull quotes, round numbered steps, a centred call to action, questions that open with a `+`.
blocks/surface.name: surface

cover/display.line: The top of a page as a poster — the eyebrow in the display face, a large muted subtitle, the picture or clip under both, a ruled byline.
cover/display.name: display

cover/page.line: A top for a site whose pages say something — the title, then a standfirst in the text colour a size up, and nothing about when or who. On a page with no cover the standfirst is the page's own first paragraph; on a post it is the cover's subtitle, and the byline is one quiet line under it with no rule.

refs.took: a page opens on its title and its first sentence — nothing says when it was written or by whom
the standfirst: one sentence a size up under the headline, before the body starts

cover/page.name: page

cover/path.line: The top of a reference page — a tracked accent eyebrow, a muted deck, the cover image in the column, a ruled byline.
cover/path.name: path

cover/plain.line: A cover that stays quiet — the eyebrow a small line in the display face, sentence case and muted, room for a badge beside it; the subtitle muted under the title; the picture at twice the radius.
cover/plain.name: plain

cover/quiet.line: The one place a reading theme raises its voice — a tracked accent eyebrow, a muted deck, the cover image in the column, a ruled byline.
cover/quiet.name: quiet

masthead/bar.line: A sticky translucent bar — the name or logo in the display face and the menu, blurring what scrolls under it, opaque once stuck. No tagline.
masthead/bar.name: bar

masthead/centered.line: A nameplate — the name centred and set large in the display face, the one big thing in the header; the tagline muted under it when the site sets one; the menu centred under them in a strip between two hairlines that run the page's width. On a phone the menu is its button, centred under the name, and one rule closes the header.

menu-button.description: Keep the Menu button on a phone. Off, a menu of six items or fewer is a row under the name that scrolls sideways; a longer one is behind the button either way.

refs.took: the name is the header: centred, set large in the display face, nothing beside it
a centred nameplate is the only large thing in the header — everything else is small and at the edges
the menu as a strip between two full-width rules, so the page starts under a line, not under a name

masthead/centered.name: centered

masthead/nameplate.line: A quiet nameplate — the name in the heading face, a muted tagline under it, the menu right; sentence case, hairline, small.

menu-button.description: Keep the Menu button on a phone. Off, a menu of six items or fewer is a row under the name that scrolls sideways; a longer one is behind the button either way.

settings.label: Tagline
settings.info: One line under the name. Defaults to the site's own description.

masthead/nameplate.name: nameplate

masthead/plain.line: Base's header as it comes — the name or logo in the display face at the left, the menu small at the right, one hairline under; a link that leaves the site is drawn as an outlined button.

menu-button.description: Keep the Menu button on a phone. Off, a menu of six items or fewer is a row under the name that scrolls sideways; a longer one is behind the button either way.

masthead/plain.name: plain

masthead/title-bar.line: A one-line title bar — name, rule, tagline, menu; a path, not a nameplate, and a `src` link to the repository last in the menu.

menu-button.description: Keep the Menu button on a phone. Off, a menu of six items or fewer is a row under the name that scrolls sideways; a longer one is behind the button either way.

settings.label: Tagline
settings.info: One line beside the name. Defaults to the site's own description.

settings.label: Source repository
settings.info: Linked from the masthead as `src`. A documentation site whose source is not one click away is documentation nobody corrects.

masthead/title-bar.name: title-bar

list/grid.line: An archive for a type that is its pictures — the heading, the count and the filter row as `list/ruled` sets them, then every entry as its cover cropped to one frame, with the title, date and first term under it; the grid breaks at each year with a rule that carries the year. It draws its own tiles, not the `entries` piece's rows.

refs.took: one crop for every tile, so the grid reads as a wall; the title and the discipline under each
a catalogue of covers at one size, the year beside the title under each
the grid broken at each turn of the date by a heading across it, so a wall of pictures stays a timeline

list/grid.name: grid

list/plain.line: An archive as a heading and its entries — and, for a type the site declares, one line under the heading that says what the list holds, counted and dated from the entries, then the type's own sentence.
list/plain.name: plain

list/ruled.line: An archive as a heading, an intro and the terms as a filter row set between two rules — each term a link with its count, the one the reader is on marked; a term's page keeps the row with its taxonomy as the heading's kicker.

refs.took: the disciplines as a filter row over the work, counts beside them
heading, one line of intro, the labels as filters, then the list
the category strip set between two rules

list/ruled.name: ruled

entries/cards.line: A grid of hairline cards — the cover on each, scaling under the pointer; the first term and the date in small caps; the title in the display face.
entries/cards.name: cards

entries/index.line: A list as an index — each entry one line, the title in the text face, a dotted leader carrying the eye to the date, which hangs in the column's right margin; under a year's heading the date drops the year.

refs.took: every entry is one line — its date and its title, nothing under it
the dot leader that carries the eye from a title across to its number
the right margin as the place for the small matter beside the line

entries/index.name: index

entries/ledger.line: A list as a ledger — ruled rows, the title at sub-heading size, a small muted line under it (the first term, and the entry's own mark — a session, a version), the date at the right.
entries/ledger.name: ledger

entries/list.line: A list of posts read by title — the title in the heading face and balanced, the date under it, the excerpt a step down from the prose.
entries/list.name: list

entries/rows.line: A list of posts as ruled rows — the date, the title in the heading face, the excerpt muted under it.
entries/rows.name: rows

post-foot/band.line: The end of a post as one band under a rule — terms as pills, the markdown twin as `↓ source`, both in the UI face.
post-foot/band.name: band

post-foot/line.line: One small line under a rule — the terms as muted outline pills, the Markdown twin with a down arrow, both brightening to the text colour on hover.
post-foot/line.name: line

post-foot/pills.line: Terms as outlined pills — the end of a post under a rule, the pills in the display face, the markdown twin a dotted text link beside them.
post-foot/pills.name: pills

post-foot/ruled.line: The end of a post as one ruled band — terms as bordered `#tags`, the markdown twin as `↓ source`.
post-foot/ruled.name: ruled

footer/close.line: One line on a dark ground — the footer note at the left, the footer menu and social links in the middle, a status note at the right; the page's scheme flipped in one declaration.

settings.label: Status note
settings.info: The right end of the footer's line — `0 KB JS · 18 rules`. A claim the site makes, in its own words. Markdown.

footer/close.name: close

footer/colophon.line: A last band ending on the name set huge — the site's description large beside the menu, social and office lists, then the wordmark, then the note under a hairline.

settings.label: Offices
settings.info: [{ label, url }] in the footer: where the studio is. A city and a map link, or an address and a mailto.

footer/colophon.name: colophon

footer/index.line: The site as a map — the name with its description beside it, then equal columns across the whole width, each under a heading with a hairline beneath it; Index (the archives and the footer menu), a column per small taxonomy, Elsewhere. The footer note closes it under a hairline. Right for a studio or a product with sections; wrong for a person with one list.

refs.took: headings in the text colour and links muted, so the eye reads the columns before the items
columns of one width, a small heading over each, and a bottom row that keeps to the same left edge
each section's heading ruled beneath, so a column is a list under a label and not a stack of links

footer/index.name: index

footer/line.line: A hairline and one quiet band — the footer menu, the social row, a note, the site's name. Muted until pointed at.

roomy.description: A step more padding and a shorter line; the menu's items a space further apart.

quiet-links.description: Every link in the footer plain and inheriting its colour — the note's and a plugin's, not only the menu's.

footer/line.name: line

home/bands.line: Full-bleed bands, dark and light — the hero with a showreel behind a display-size headline, each `##` section a numbered band, the newest posts last.

settings.label: Bands
settings.info: The front page's sections as alternating dark and light bands, starting with the hero; `off` keeps the whole page in the reader's scheme.

home/bands.name: bands

home/index.line: The front page is the ruled index — a line of intro, then every entry newest first in groups by year, the year set in the margin; the page's `##` sections follow as an afterword.

settings.label: Entries on the front page
settings.info: How many of each list the front page indexes, newest first. The way to the whole archive is under the list either way.

refs.took: the archive is the front page; a sentence above it and nothing else
one list, every entry, no hero
the year as a running mark over its entries

home/index.name: index

home/portfolio.line: The front page is the work — a line of intro, then a grid of the listed type's covers, each whole inside a frame they share and standing on one line over a wall label; the page's `##` sections follow as an afterword.

settings.label: Works on the front page
settings.info: How many of the listed type the front page shows, newest first — the type the header menu names first. The way to the whole archive is under the grid either way.

refs.took: the work is the front page; the studio's own words come after it
every picture whole inside a cell every work shares, never cropped, so a tall one and a wide one sit as equals
the caption as a wall label: the title, then the year and one fact, small, under the work

home/portfolio.name: portfolio

home/split.line: A product page — one big centred sentence, the film under it, a button; then every `##` section a band with its heading beside its content; the site's lists as bands; the last section a dark close.

settings.label: Hero button
settings.info: The word on the button under the front page's headline. With no link below, no button is drawn.

settings.label: Hero button link
settings.info: Where that button goes — a Start page, the docs, an install guide. Site-relative or absolute; empty draws no button.

home/split.name: split

feature/facts.line: A case as three bands — the cover with a facts strip under it (every `role: fact` field, then the year), the body with its sections numbered, and a close with the call to action beside the next one.

settings.label: Call to action
settings.info: The line at the end of every feature page — "Have something to make?" With no link below, nothing is shown.

settings.label: Call to action link
settings.info: Where the button under it goes — a contact page, a mailto:, a form. Site-relative or absolute.

feature/facts.name: facts

feature/log.line: A dated entry as a reading page — the kicker above the title, the date and every `role: fact` field as one ruled strip under it, and the entry after it as one row at the end.
feature/log.name: log

feature/release.line: A release as a reading page — the version above the title with a badge when it breaks, the date and the facts as one byline, and the releases either side of it at the end.
feature/release.name: release

notes/cards.line: Footnotes as base shows them — a card on hover or focus, in the theme's surface — and the ruled list at the end.

on-page.description: The card on the page's own background rather than the surface colour — a theme whose surface is for code.

notes/cards.name: cards

notes/plain.line: Footnotes left to base — its card on hover, unmarked reference numbers — and the ruled list at the end in small type.
notes/plain.name: plain

notes/sidenotes.line: Footnotes in the margin — once there is room beside the column, each note stands next to its line, always visible; the list at the end is the printed version.
notes/sidenotes.name: sidenotes

toc/block.line: A contents list at the top of a post, in flow — two columns once there is room, one on a phone; it marks where the reader is in Chrome 140+.

settings.label: Contents depth
settings.info: How deep the contents list on a post goes: 2 is section headings only, 3 includes their sub-headings, 0 turns it off.

toc/block.name: block

wall/marquee.line: Marks that scroll — on one baseline under a hairline, softened until pointed at; a `marquee` wall runs, pauses under the pointer, and stands still on a phone or under reduced motion.
wall/marquee.name: marquee

wall/row.line: Marks in a row under a hairline — a `marquee` wall is the same row, still.

plain-title.description: The wall's title as written, in the display face — not tracked capitals in the UI face.

wall/row.name: row

motion/glide.line: The title glides between pages — the page swaps at once and only the title moves (a cross-document view transition); a reading-progress line and scroll entrances are switches.

progress.description: A thin line in the accent across the top of a post, filling as it is read (scroll-driven; none in Firefox).

reveal.description: Listed entries, stats, the front page's steps and the wall's marks rise into place as they scroll in, and numbers count up to their value. Translate only, never opacity; still under reduced motion.

motion/glide.name: glide

motion/still.line: Nothing moves between pages — the next page is swapped in, never held for a transition; numbers counting up as they scroll in is a switch.

count.description: A stat's figure counts up from zero as it scrolls in, painted over the real text, which stays in the page. Under `@supports`; still under reduced motion.

motion/still.name: still

editorial.line: A reading page — a text serif on paper, notes in the margin, a quiet nameplate, posts read by title.

notebook.line: A writer's notebook — a centred nameplate, the site as a ruled index, pages that open on their first sentence, blocks in ink.

refs.took: a writer's front page as a list of what they wrote, the headline at a display face's regular weight
a long-form site in the text colour alone, the index as the front door

portfolio.line: A portfolio — the work whole on the front page, archives as walls of covers by year, a centred nameplate, the footer a map.

refs.took: the work is the front page; the studio's words come after it
every picture whole inside a frame every work shares

studio.line: A studio's site — full-bleed bands and a showreel, cases as cards and three-band pages, a name set huge at the foot.

technical.line: Reference docs — a title bar, code and tables as the content, a contents block, posts as ruled rows.
